findings.summary: Read-back capacity was smaller than publication capacity. artifact-binding put the artifact body on the wire as base64, so a read request grew to about 4/3 of the artifact while every operation shares one fixed 8 MiB input ceiling. An artifact that put() accepted could therefore be unreadable, and an already published, already referenced artifact could not be read back at all.
findings.user_visible_consequence: Completed work could not be resumed: a worker that had written its receipt could not read it back on re-entry.
findings.reproduction: 6.25 MiB artifact: put() succeeds, the pre-migration get() succeeds, M3's get() raises 'bridge input exceeds 8 MiB'; a real worker re-entry fails.

findings.observed: The unchanged workflow test returned from the graph without a terminal key and raised KeyError('terminal') at line 54, with no check-complete, evaluate or seal before it.

acceptance_attempt.blocker: ZCODE_TRANSPORT: Native output closed (doctor exit 2). The ZCode app-server exits immediately.
acceptance_attempt.blocker_cause: SEE CORRECTION. The cause is not the host install. Two parts, both on our side: (a) FIXED - ZCode 3.12.3 ships the app-server's built-in provider catalogue at <Resources>/config/provider/zcode-builtin.json, while the app-server only derives <script dir>/provider/zcode-builtin.json and a source-tree-relative ../../../../../config/provider/zcode-builtin.json (which normalises to /config/provider/zcode-builtin.json). Both miss, so it exits 1 before emitting any protocol. The file is present; only its location moved. (b) NOT FIXED - the same build removed workspace/readState, which this transport calls first, and session/create now answers settings.model={"available": []} with no current selection.

adaptation_applied.what: Two changes. (1) native_transport.py now owns what every native transport shares - spawning one host process, the line-delimited JSON request/reply loop, the routing-only trace, answering the host's own client-directed requests, error classification, bindings, the four evidence files and session close - and an adapter supplies protocol hooks only: ident/envelope, respond, classify, notification. native_dsh.py drops its own reader, request loop, process lifecycle and binding; native_zcode.py drops its framing. Both declare the shared module in TRANSPORT_FILES, so a fix to the shared mechanics stays reviewable as a transport change for every host. (2) The ZCode transport is adapted to the 3.12.3 surface: workspace/readState is no longer called, the snapshot comes straight from session/resume or session/create, the handshake every snapshot carries is checked instead of assumed, and selection is applied only through session/setModel with persistAsWorkspaceLastUsed:false and confirmed from the host's own report. The transport no longer assembles a provider runtime config for the host.
adaptation_applied.verified: go vet exit 0. Python suite 206 OK (199 before; +3 host-side, +4 shared-boundary). doctor --provider dsh PASSES end to end through the shared boundary, so extracting it did not change DSH behaviour. doctor --provider zcode still fails, but at a different point - see remaining_adaptation.

The session is created, the ZCode Protocol v1 handshake passes and the settings snapshot is read; the host itself reports no selected model.

The driver binary did not move across any of them: sha256 a4d9ac94... throughout.

remaining_adaptation.what: Nothing remains for doctor-zcode: it is re-measured PASS on the current candidate (see blocker_cleared). What remained for the native ZCode path as a whole was the reverse interaction channel (interaction/requestProviderRuntimeHeaders). It is now measured to be required rather than merely assigned a unit, and the transport answers it. Measured: with the interaction refused the turn fails in the model_creation phase with no model call; with it answered a real turn completes (turn.completed, resultType success, one model request). The answer comes from the host's own provisioning index through the host's own cipher (commit d2f4847), so ZCODE_INTERACTION_REQUIRED now covers only the two interactions that really are user decisions. See scope_boundary_unchanged for the two reading errors this corrects and for what stays open.
remaining_adaptation.judged_not_assumed: The delivery is judged from the host's own answers, not from our own success: session/create reports the provider it selected and the models it advertises, and the "entitled:false" control returns the registry to available 0 and current null, so the fill is caused by the delivery. The revision is judged against the agent's own log line for the same launch, which matches the computed value character for character.
remaining_adaptation.what_is_empty: Unchanged and still empty by design: the built-in release contributes 20 templateRules and 8 entitlement-gated account:* providerRules, and the personal provider document has 0 rules. The selectable set is the account handoff, which is why a launcher has to make it.
remaining_adaptation.impact: doctor-zcode was a required item for every unit, so nothing could close while it failed. That specific obstacle is now removed.
remaining_adaptation.determination: Root cause established and fixed on our side: the transport never made the account provider handoff the host makes, and on the same path it bound a model without the reasoning level the host requires and dismissed a reported selection that carried options. All three are fixed; the earlier disposition ("blocked, no code change") is withdrawn as falsified. The unit conclusion stays FAIL for the two findings recorded above, which this work does not touch and does not claim to.

remaining_adaptation.scope_boundary_unchanged: This clears the probe item only, which makes 0 model calls, so it does NOT show that a real turn completes. An earlier revision of this field said a real turn still needs the reverse interaction channel; that was then corrected to "unmeasured rather than established", and the correction is now itself falsified by measurement. Corrected reading: in host mode the app-server's provider runtime headers port (bundle: createProviderRuntimeHeadersPort) reports shouldRefreshBeforeModelRequest() true unconditionally, so before every model request the app-server asks its client for the request auth and abandons the turn when the reply lacks headersApplied/requestAuth. The claim that the method occurs in the bundle once, as a protocol-table name, with no client-side sender, was a search miss: the sender is that port, and its response is a strict union discriminated on headersApplied. Measured both ways: answering -32601 fails the turn in the model_creation phase with no model call, and answering per the contract reaches turn.completed with resultType success. Implemented: the transport answers it from the same provisioning index the account overlay is built from, through the host's own cipher (zcode_credential.mjs: sha256 of a fixed fallback string, aes-256-gcm, no keychain and no user decision), so it no longer refuses the interaction; a provider with no provisioned credential is reported as headersApplied false rather than invented. Proved through this transport and not through a probe: one real turn completes with answer.raw.txt {"ok": true} and interaction-status.json provider-runtime-headers-applied. Two model calls were spent in total, on the owner's explicit instruction to make ZCode really work end to end, which overrides the section 12.5 default. Credential values are now read, which the earlier wording explicitly denied; only this account's own provisioned value is read, and it never enters evidence, because Client.answer records the method and the status only. Still open: standalone mode (the --prompt/TUI path, which reads credentials through its own port and needs no client at all) is unreachable on this machine, because the store holds no account-provider:<id>:identity record that standalone entitlement requires, so a standalone registry comes up unentitled and the turn stops at "Select a model before continuing"; only standalone login writes that record. Nothing about DSH is measured by this.

blocker_cleared.observed: {"ok": true} with model_calls 0, selection model {"modelId":"GLM-5.3","providerId":"account:bigmodel-individual-coding-plan"} and reasoning_effort "max"; the binding names both provider-configuration variables. The same command with an explicit --model reports the same shape.
blocker_cleared.earlier_conclusion_withdrawn: "doctor-zcode cannot pass by configuring anything on this machine ... no code change is made" is withdrawn. It is falsified by measurement, not by argument: the delivery it called unavailable is a client-to-agent protocol method this launcher can send itself, and every input it needs is readable from the host's own files. Nothing was installed, no permission was granted, no credential was read and no host configuration was modified; the probes wrote only inside .harness, and the repair itself changes only the development driver sources under runtime/langgraph/ together with this record.
blocker_cleared.root_cause: The app-server keeps no provider registry of its own: it starts with an empty account source and the account provider configuration arrives as the provider/updateAccountConfig call the host normally makes after provider/model readiness. This launcher never made that call, so session/create answered settings.model={"current": null, "available": []} and the transport refused rather than inventing a selection. The earlier attribution to host account state stays withdrawn; the missing piece was on our side, and it was a missing protocol step, not an installation or an authorization.
blocker_cleared.revision_rule: The delivered basedOnZCodeBuiltinRevision must equal the agent's own resolved revision exactly: ProviderRegistryService abandons its refresh when o.basedOnZCodeBuiltinRevision !== n.zcodeBuiltinRevision (zcode.cjs, ProviderRegistryService.#v), so a delivery that is even slightly off is discarded in silence. That revision is "zcode-builtin:" + the catalogue's revision + ":" + sha256(path.resolve(activeCatalogue)); the hash is of the resolved path, not of the contents. Verified by computing it and matching the agent's own log: computed zcode-builtin:28:8f54ff88... equals the zcode_protocol.provider_registry.ready accountRevision the agent logged for the same launch (pinned-delivery.py). The same rule explains the three hashes seen earlier: c1a2fc01... is our previous spawn at ~/.zcode/v2/runtime/provider/darwin-aarch64/0.0.0-dev/endpoint-78d7c3be.../zcode-builtin.json, a7b54955... is the desktop host at the same path under 3.12.3, and 8f54ff88... is the bundle's own catalogue path.
blocker_cleared.ownership: The app-server's bootstrap rewrites ZCODE_BUILTIN_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE to a path it derives unless ZCODE_PERSONAL_PROVIDER_CONFIG_FILE is named too, which is why the previous fix moved the failure forward without making the catalogue the launcher's. Naming both pins the path, and only then can the launcher know the revision at all.
blocker_cleared.provisioning_index: Which account providers the host can use is read from the key names of ~/.zcode/v2/credentials.json (account-provider:coding-plan:<provider>:account:<identity>:api-key) and matched against the catalogue's declared account rules. Values there are encrypted secrets and are never read. This host's index holds exactly two, which is the same providerCount 2 the desktop host reports for the same account. The same index is what the client is asked for later: before every model request the app-server calls interaction/requestProviderRuntimeHeaders and needs the credential for the provider it is about to use (see scope_boundary_unchanged).
blocker_cleared.preferred_provider: The plan the host itself selected is read from ~/.zcode/v2/setting.json (providerFamilyDomain plus the family's connection kind) and matched to a provider on the catalogue's own declared accountType and mode, never on the spelling of an id. With no --model the doctor now binds account:bigmodel-individual-coding-plan, the same plan the desktop app itself uses, instead of whichever provider the credential file lists first.
blocker_cleared.negative_control: The fill is caused by the delivery, not by anything else: the same call with entitled false returns the registry to available 0 and current null (deliver-provider-config.py, attempt D).
blocker_cleared.second_and_third_defects: Two further defects on the same path were unreachable until the registry was filled, and both are fixed. (1) session/setModel takes an object and refuses one whose options.reasoningLevel is absent, and the level must be one of that model's advertised values; the transport now binds the requested effort when one was asked for and the host's own advertised default otherwise (available[].reasoning.defaultLevel, falling back to the first advertised value, mirroring the host). The string form is not an option: the protocol schema rejects it with "model: Invalid input: expected object, received string" (reasoning-level.py). (2) selected_model() required a reported current to be exactly {providerId, modelId}, but a configured host reports it with the bound options, so a host that had a selection was read as having none.
blocker_cleared.scope_boundary_unchanged: This clears the probe item only, which makes 0 model calls, so it does NOT show that a real turn completes. An earlier revision of this field said a real turn still needs the reverse interaction channel; that is corrected here as unmeasured rather than established. Reading the bundle: the agent opens and parses the shared account store itself (<baseDir>/.zcode/v2/credentials.json) and composes the account key as account-provider:coding-plan:<providerId>:account:<identity>:api-key, i.e. exactly the index this transport reads, so account auth does not obviously require a reverse request; and interaction/requestProviderRuntimeHeaders occurs once in the bundle, as a protocol-table name, with no client-side sender site found. The reverse channel stays refused by design with ZCODE_INTERACTION_REQUIRED, which plan section 12.4 delivers separately as G2d, but it is NOT shown to be what stands in the way. Settling it costs one model call, which section 12.5 does not let this work spend on its own authority.
